The University of Rhode Island College of Nursing’s Accelerated Online R.N. to B.S. program is dedicated to providing an education that will broaden your view of the world and create opportunities to transform healthcare in your own community. Building upon your clinical experience, the R.N. to B.S. program expands your scientific knowledge base, giving you a set of skills that allows you to integrate clinical practice, scientific inquiry and critical, creative thinking. You’ll graduate fully prepared for a whole new world of healthcare opportunities. Progression and Graduation Requirements Students are expected to achieve a C or higher in all required courses. In addition, students must maintain a minimum GPA of 2.2 to progress through and graduate from the College of Nursing.

Students who achieve less than a grade of C must repeat the course, obtaining a C grade or higher, before progressing in the nursing curriculum. Permission to retake the course will be granted on a space-available basis only. Even if successfully repeated, the initial grade remains on record as the first unsuccessful attempt. There are no further allowances for repeating a NUR course, and any subsequent NUR coursework of C- or below will result in dismissal. If the student should achieve a C- or less in two NUR courses in a single session or semester, he or she will be immediately dismissed from the College of Nursing. A total of 120 credits is required to earn a B.S. in Nursing. This includes program specific courses as well as general education requirements. R.N. to B.S. Overview.
There is renewed interest in ocean acoustics due to undersea defense applications as well as concerns about the effects of anthropogenic noise (e.g., from offshore wind farms) on marine animals.
The US Navy recently began a five-year, $2.4 billion investment in industrial base and workforce development support, including nearly $750 million in FY23 for the submarine industrial base.
In the realm of offshore renewable energy, the US has a goal of installing 30 gigawatts of offshore wind farms by 2030, or enough to power more than 10 million homes for a year.
One of the major objectives of the graduate certificate is to provide an option for students from engineering, oceanography, or other fields who would like to have graduate preparation in ocean acoustics.
Many of the courses below are already offered in a hybrid mode indicated by the asterisks.
We propose that an adequate number of hybrid courses be available for this certificate.
A concern for the public and environmentalists is the ocean noise impact of wind farm construction on marine mammals and fish.
Both the defense and offshore wind industries need people with expertise in ocean acoustics.

URI is uniquely qualified to deliver this graduate certificate in ocean acoustics to meet the knowledge needs of these workforces.
URI's mission includes a commitment to high-quality education, community engagement, and solving the world’s most important challenges.

Health and Disease: Teetering on Disaster Many countries have undergone a shift from acute infectious to chronic diseases and this transformation is often fostered by changes in social norms, the economic climate, and political infrastructure, often generating issues of public importance and concern. Epidemiological methods, grounded in overarching ethical theories, provide a useful approach to evaluate these changes. This course will introduce students to relevant theories of population health and ethics, and then apply these frameworks to modern case studies.
